evidence: src/delivery/tracking/dtos/update-route.dto.ts: UpdateRouteDto { @IsString() id: string; @IsString() courierId?: string; @IsString() orderId?: string; }
Both files import only IsString from class-validator and are used together by tracking.controller.ts and tracking.service.ts, so they form one coherent group of route inputs.

The field checks are repeated in UpdateRouteDto instead of building it from CreateRouteDto (e.g. PartialType), and the optional fields have no @IsOptional(). This is minor and not counted as a violation.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module covers one concern: the input shapes for creating and updating a tracking route. Both files are plain class-validator DTOs that follow the same pattern, with no business logic, persistence code or unrelated concerns. The @IsString() checks on courierId and orderId are repeated in both files instead of building the update DTO from the create DTO (for example with PartialType). With only two fields this is a small repeat, not a real duplicated rule, so it is not counted as a failure. Also worth noting: UpdateRouteDto marks courierId and orderId as optional but has no @IsOptional(), so validation will reject a request that leaves either out. That is a correctness bug rather than a cohesion violation, but it shows the two copies have already drifted apart.
